summary: Web of Worlds is a Metaverse Standards Forum direction for making virtual worlds addressable and linkable with ordinary web machinery, announced by the Forum's 3D Web Interoperability Working Group on 2 June 2026. Its whole normative surface is three small OpenAPI files at version 0.0.1 — a world API, an asset API and a user manifest API — plus a README table of five core requirements saying a world is joined, followed, previewed, saved and shared by its URL. It is strong on one idea, that a world is a URL and its parts hang off that URL, and it does that well. Almost everything else a working group would look for is absent rather than wrong: no units, no scale, no up axis, no bounds, no coordinate reference system, no signature, no destination on a portal, and no way for one world to contain another. The first trap is that none of the three files uses a single normative keyword and no schema requires a single property, so an empty object validates as a World, a User, a Node, a Portal, a View and a Spatial descriptor alike; a team that reads the whitepaper will expect decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, selective disclosure, glTF, USD and X3D, and will find none of them in the machine-readable text. The second trap is now demonstrated rather than predicted: the world README puts the scene graph under /wow/scene/, the machine-readable file puts it under /wow/spatial/{spatialID}, and the project's own reference implementation, simpleWorlds, publishes a third OpenAPI file that serves /wow/scene/node/{nodeId}. The specification and its reference implementation disagree about the normative graph path, so two good-faith servers cannot talk.

coverage.note: The core of the subject: a world is a URL, joined, followed and previewed by URL fragment, and its parts hang off that same URL as URL/wow/world and URL/wow/user/4182. The whitepaper states the idea directly and the world README turns it into the five core requirements.

Node.children is an array of embedded Node objects, so a subtree is carried inline, while Node.parent is a bare integer, so the same relationship is also expressible by reference; neither is required, no precedence is stated, and nothing says what a server should do when both are present. The project's own integration served a flat identifier-reference node instead, and before that divergence was declared a write with embedded children was answered 200 OK with its whole subtree silently deleted. coverage.note: No world declares units, scale or extent. The World schema carries a label, an age restriction, a licence, a cost, a version and a duration and nothing dimensional, so metre scale is an assumption that is never stated and a renderer has nothing to compute a bound from. coverage.note: Web of Worlds describes worlds and the ways in and out of them. How a client presents a world against a camera view of the room is the client's own affair and the API says nothing about it.
The API is about a world's description and a visitor's session, not about reading the visitor's face or body from a sensor.

A world advertises how it is moved through as one free-text string beside its avatar and gravity settings. That is a hint for a person choosing a world, not a declaration a client can act on: no walkable surface, no bounds, no spawn points, nothing that tells an arriving client where a body may stand.

coverage.note: Worlds are addressed by URL and described by a manifest of aspects. Nothing is published as a reusable unit of logic under a name that has to keep resolving, so there is no namespace here and no protection against a second author reusing a name.

sources.title: Web of Worlds OpenSpatialWorld API specification
sources.quote: presence: type: object properties: avatar: type: string navigation: type: string gravity: type: string

coverage.note: The API is where a receiving client would learn what a world is before entering it, and the description it gets covers cost, version, duration, technology and presence. There is no content rating, no review record and no statement of who has checked the world or its contents.

sources.title: Web of Worlds OpenSpatialWorld API specification
sources.quote: technology: type: object properties: webXR-immersive: type: string description: "WebXR session profile"

coverage.note: A world may carry a GeoPose that puts it somewhere on Earth. That is a placement, not a declared map with a version, and the API publishes no transform between two maps of a place.

The geographic hook is a single GeoPose: one latitude, longitude and height with angles. A point is not an area, so a client cannot test whether a world applies where the client is; it can only be told where the world claims to be.
